task: Lean regression sanity check re-running iteration_35's /print-tags mobile matrix (390x844) after a code-review report whose 'critical' items were confirmed false positives (missing-hook-deps on stable imports, sessionStorage CSRF mislabeled as localStorage auth token, PEP-8-correct `is True`/`is None` flagged as literal-is bugs, vite.config.ts console.warn flagged as prod code). No application code was changed.
summary: Re-ran all 6 acceptance criteria from iteration_35 against the public preview URL on 390x844. 'print-tags-controls-full-width-mobile' reran clean unchanged. The other 3 persisted checks ('print-tags-preview-grid-scrollable', 'print-tags-long-price-title-no-overlap', 'print-tags-open-pdf-button-works') initially FAILED on rerun -- not an app regression: they referenced hardcoded fixture item ids that iteration_35's own cleanup step deleted at the end of that run (confirmed via authenticated GET /api/inventory/{id} -> 404 'Item not found' for both ids). This is a test-artifact fragility, not a code bug. Fixed by rewriting the 3 checks to create their own tscheck-* fixture items via the app's authenticated POST /api/inventory at the start of each run (matching the fixture-creation pattern already used elsewhere in the suite, e.g. condition-edit-persists-after-reload) and delete them at the end. Re-ran after the fix: all 3 passed with the same layout numbers as iteration_35 (grid scrollWidth 809 vs clientWidth 358, price/QR no overlap at £225.00, 2-line title clamp, PDF ready toast with zero console errors). Confirmed zero tscheck-* residue in inventory afterward. No application/product code was touched -- only the test checks' own fixture-creation logic.
action_items: The persisted browser checks 'print-tags-preview-grid-scrollable', 'print-tags-long-price-title-no-overlap', and 'print-tags-open-pdf-button-works' previously hardcoded fixture item ids from a one-off seed, which broke on rerun once those fixtures were cleaned up. They now self-seed tscheck-* fixtures and clean up after themselves, making them rerun-safe going forward -- no further action needed, noted for traceability only.
